No-paid signoff finalization can still mutate stale context without a drift check. Evidence: `dontpanic finalize` calls `signed_off_finalizer.finalize_signed_off_feature` directly in [cli.py](/Users/bayesian/Documents/GitHub/DontPanic/scripts/dontpanic_orchestrate/cli.py:760), and the finalizer writes signoff/features state in [signed_off_finalizer.py](/Users/bayesian/Documents/GitHub/DontPanic/scripts/dontpanic_orchestrate/signed_off_finalizer.py:183) and [signed_off_finalizer.py](/Users/bayesi

Non-additive `decisions.jsonl` edits can be misclassified as additive-only. Evidence: `_decision_ids` tracks only ordered IDs, and `_decisions_change` treats any ID-prefix plus append as `ADDITIVE_LEDGER`; an in-memory check with changed file hash and IDs `("D001") -> ("D001","D002")` returned `additive_ledger`. Recommendation: fingerprint each decision line/content, and only classify as additive when all existing lines are byte-identical and new lines are appended.

Tests do not cover required gate-state drift or actual supervisor call-boundary behavior. Evidence: `test_plan_drift_f009.py` covers the pure reconciliation helper and plan/frontmatter edits, but has no `gate-state.json` case and no dispatch-volley test proving a mocked implementer/auditor call is skipped after a concurrent edit. Recommendation: add integration-style supervisor tests for implementer, auditor, and finalization boundaries, including `gate-state.json`. Checks run: $ PYTHONDONTWRITE
